texts.li: Same spot by the door, same time every evening. {A_nameDef} came dragging in from a long shift, and {X_definite} was already up and waiting.
At the sound of {A_nameDef}'s footsteps on the path, {X_definite} came running so fast {X_pronoun} nearly went over.
{A_nameDef} sat on the step, too tired to unlace {A_possessive} boots, and {X_definite} leaned {X_possessive} whole weight against {A_objective}.
Some time in the night {X_definite} climbed onto {A_nameDef}'s bed, and in the morning {A_nameDef} woke pinned under the blankets.
Every night {X_definite} turns three slow circles and drops across {A_nameDef}'s feet. {A_nameDef} hasn't had warm toes this reliably in years.
These days {A_nameDef} sleeps badly without {X_definite} snoring at the foot of the bed.
One glance away, and the best piece of meat was gone from {A_nameDef}'s plate. Across the room, {X_definite} chewed and would not meet anyone's eye.
{A_nameDef} set {A_possessive} bowl down to scratch an itch. When {A_pronoun} looked back, {X_definite} had {X_possessive} whole face in it.
Half of {A_nameDef}'s dinner went out the door with {X_definite}. {A_nameDef} gave chase for three steps, then sat back down and ate the other half faster.
A dead rat on {A_nameDef}'s pillow, still warm, and {X_definite} sitting beside it waiting to be praised.
{A_nameDef} pulled on {A_possessive} boot this morning and found the back half of a mouse in it, left there by {X_definite}.
{A_nameDef} made a fuss of {X_definite} once for a dead squirrel on the doorstep. Since then there has been a dead bird or rat there most mornings.
"Stay." {A_nameDef} must have said it two hundred times this afternoon, and by sunset {X_definite} was staying about half the time.
After a week of patience and kitchen scraps, {X_definite} finally comes when {A_nameDef} whistles, and also when anyone else does.
{A_nameDef} is teaching {X_definite} to fetch. So far {X_pronoun} chases the stick, lies down with it and chews it.
{A_nameDef} sat behind the storehouse with {A_possessive} head in {A_possessive} hands. After a while {X_definite} came and leaned against {A_objective}, and didn't move until {A_nameDef} did.
For days now {A_nameDef} has barely said a word, and in all that time {X_definite} has not left {A_possessive} side.
Out by the pens, {A_nameDef} cried into the warm side of {X_definite} until the worst had passed.
{A_nameDef} skipped supper and lay facing the wall. Some time later {X_definite} pushed the door open with {X_possessive} head and lay down beside the bed with a heavy sigh.
{A_nameDef}'s spare boots are a damp heap of leather now, and {X_definite} is asleep on top of it.
A trail of stuffing led from {A_nameDef}'s chewed-through bedding to {X_definite}'s sleeping spot.
The spoon {A_nameDef} spent a week carving was in splinters under the table, with {X_definite} still working on the handle.
{A_nameDef} opened the storeroom and found {X_definite} sitting in a torn sack of vegetables, very round and not at all sorry.
Somebody left the larder door open. By the time {A_nameDef} noticed, {X_definite} had eaten a fair hole in the raw food.
{A_nameDef} followed a trail of gnawed peel from the storeroom to the barn, where {X_definite} lay on {X_possessive} side with a swollen belly.

ColonyCouncil.EncounterDef.label: a child at play with an animal

texts.li: {A_nameDef} chased {X_definite} round the yard all afternoon, then {X_definite} chased {A_nameDef}, and at sundown the two of them lay flat in the dirt.
{A_nameDef} tied a ribbon round {X_definite}'s neck and declared {X_objective} a knight of the colony. By supper the knight had eaten the ribbon.
{A_nameDef} built {X_definite} a house out of sticks and an old blanket, and spent the evening trying to coax {X_objective} inside.
All afternoon {A_nameDef} held up fingers in front of {X_definite}, trying to teach {X_objective} to count.
{A_nameDef} isn't the one who looks after {X_definite}, but lately {X_pronoun} follows {A_nameDef} from room to room and sleeps across {A_possessive} doorway.
At every meal now {X_definite} waits under {A_nameDef}'s chair, though {A_nameDef} has never once fed {X_objective}.
{A_nameDef} can't work out why {X_definite} has picked {A_objective}. Today {X_pronoun} walked {A_objective} to the latrine and waited outside.
Someone passing the pens heard {A_nameDef} telling {X_definite} everything that has gone wrong this season.
At night, {A_nameDef} talks to {X_definite} about the things {A_pronoun} won't say at the table.
"Am I doing all right out here?" {A_nameDef} asked {X_definite}, and got a long yawn back.
Whenever {A_nameDef} walks past, {X_definite} stops what {X_pronoun} is doing and stares at {A_objective} until {A_pronoun} is out of sight.
Scraps and soft words have both been tried, and {X_definite} still goes for {A_nameDef}'s ankles on sight.
{A_nameDef} says {X_definite} waits behind the barn door for {A_objective} and no one else. It happened twice before breakfast today.
Every morning {X_definite} follows {A_nameDef} out to work and lies down just out of the way to watch.
{A_nameDef} shut {X_definite} in this morning, and half an hour later found {X_objective} waiting at the work site, muddy to the belly.
All day {A_nameDef} hauled, and all day {X_definite} was underfoot, delighted with the job.
This morning it took {X_definite} a long time to get up, and longer to manage the step. {A_nameDef} waited at the bottom and didn't say a word.
These days {X_definite} walks out to meet {A_nameDef} in the evening instead of running. But {X_pronoun} still comes.
{A_nameDef} moved {X_definite}'s bed closer to the fire and says it's because of the draft.
In the straw this morning {A_nameDef} found a heap of squalling newborns, with {X_definite} standing over them and watching {A_objective} closely.
New mouths in the barn. {A_nameDef} tried to count them under {X_definite}'s hard stare and lost track, because they would not keep still.
{A_nameDef} spent the evening in the barn naming the newborns after members of the council, while {X_definite} dozed beside them.
A traveler reached out to clap {A_nameDef} on the shoulder and found {X_definite} in the way, standing very still and watching the hand.
{A_nameDef} never asked {X_definite} to guard {A_objective}. But whenever a stranger comes near, there {X_pronoun} is, standing just in front of {A_nameDef}, as if by accident.
Words got sharp between {A_nameDef} and an outsider at the gate, and before the second sentence {X_definite} was planted between them, silent, eyes fixed on the stranger.
Well after dark, {X_definite} started making an unholy noise at nothing, and kept at it until {A_nameDef} went out in a blanket to sit with {X_objective}.
{A_nameDef} is awake because {X_definite} is awake, standing stiff-legged by the wall and staring into the dark.
{A_nameDef} lay listening to {X_definite} cry out toward the tree line, over and over, and tried not to think about what was out there.
Work stopped all over the colony when {X_indefinite} crossed the far meadow, slow and enormous. {A_nameDef} had seen {X_objective} first and called the others out to look.
{A_nameDef} looked up from {A_possessive} work and saw {X_indefinite} among the trees, looking back. Neither of them moved until {X_pronoun} turned and walked off.
{A_nameDef} watched {X_definite} drink from the stream for most of the morning and got nothing else done.
{A_nameDef} crept close enough to {X_definite} to hear {X_objective} breathe, and came back shaking and grinning.
Flat in the grass all afternoon, {A_nameDef} studied the way {X_definite} set {X_possessive} feet down and what made {X_objective} lift {X_possessive} head.
{A_nameDef} spent the morning a few paces from {X_indefinite}, near enough to count the scars on {X_possessive} hide, and that evening started pacing out ground for a pen.
First up this morning, {A_nameDef} found {X_indefinite} grazing in the mist just past the fence and stood listening to {X_objective} tear at the grass.
In the gray light before breakfast, {A_nameDef} watched {X_indefinite} step out of the trees, nose at the wet grass, and step back in.
{A_nameDef} stood very still at the well while {X_indefinite} drank from the runoff not ten paces away. The bucket grew heavy in {A_possessive} hands. {A_nameDef} didn't set it down.
{A_nameDef} gave up counting at forty. The herd, {X_indefinite} and dozens more like {X_objective}, took most of the afternoon to pass the colony.
A herd went by to the south today, {X_definite} straggling at the back. {A_nameDef} stopped work to watch and was the last one back to it.
The herd took an hour to pass, and the fence shook the whole time under {A_nameDef}'s hands.
Birdsong from the hedges all morning, and {X_indefinite} dozing on a warm rock while {A_nameDef} worked.
{A_nameDef} ate lunch on an upturned bucket and took {A_possessive} time about it, with the hedges loud with birds and {X_indefinite} poking through the new grass.
{A_nameDef} whistled back at the birds for most of the afternoon. They ignored {A_objective}, but {X_indefinite} crept out of the grass to listen.
Out past the fields {X_indefinite} called into the cold dark, and another answered from farther off. {A_nameDef} went out twice to check the gate.
{A_nameDef} lay awake listening to {X_indefinite} somewhere in the bare trees, calling and calling, and could not decide whether the sound was lonely or hungry.
The calling went on half the night. {A_nameDef} swears that at one point {X_indefinite} was right outside the fence, close enough to hear the breath between calls.
For most of the afternoon {X_indefinite} paced the far side of the fence, keeping exactly level with {A_nameDef} as {A_pronoun} worked. {A_nameDef} found a reason to finish early.
{A_nameDef} went out for firewood and came face to face with {X_indefinite} nosing at the woodpile. They both backed away slowly, and {A_nameDef} came in without the wood.
There are fresh prints right up to the fields, and {X_indefinite} lying in the shade just past them, watching {A_nameDef} work.
{A_nameDef} looked up and found {X_indefinite} low in the long grass, eyes on {A_objective}. When {A_nameDef} stood up and shouted, the animal didn't run.
At first light {A_nameDef} found a row of seedlings bitten off at the root, and {X_indefinite} at the end of it, still chewing.
{A_nameDef} chased {X_indefinite} out of the crops three times before noon. The fourth time, {A_nameDef} sat down in the dirt and let {X_objective} have the corner.
There's {X_indefinite} living under the hedge, and {X_pronoun} eats only from the rows {A_nameDef} tends.
{A_nameDef} has been leaving crusts on the same flat stone every day. Today {X_indefinite} was already waiting beside it, looking pointedly at {A_possessive} pocket.
{A_nameDef} crouched with a handful of grain held out until {A_possessive} knees ached, and at last {X_indefinite} ate from {A_possessive} palm, then bolted.
Each noon this week {A_nameDef} has split {A_possessive} lunch with {X_indefinite} beside the field, and each day {X_pronoun} sits a step closer.

ColonyCouncil.EncounterDef.label: a child meets a wild animal

texts.li: In the long grass, {X_indefinite} came right up to {A_nameDef} and sniffed {A_possessive} hair before wandering off.
The adults froze when {X_indefinite} came toward {A_nameDef}. {A_nameDef} held out half an apple, and {X_definite} took it gently and went on {X_possessive} way.
"It touched noses with me," {A_nameDef} kept saying, all the way up from the water, and that night {A_pronoun} drew {X_definite} on the wall above the bed.
By the water {A_nameDef} found prints deep enough to hold rain and wide enough to stand in, left by {X_indefinite} some time in the night.
Snapped saplings and tracks the size of serving platters led off toward the hills. {A_nameDef} followed them a hundred paces, saw {X_indefinite} through the trees, and turned back.
{A_nameDef} laid both hands flat in one of {X_definite}'s footprints, side by side, and there was still room left over.
{A_nameDef} wanted to know what {X_indefinite} felt like up close, so {A_pronoun} walked straight up and laid a hand on {X_possessive} flank while the others held their breath at the fence.
On a dare, {A_nameDef} crept up behind {X_definite} and poked {X_objective} with a stick, then stood there just long enough to watch {X_possessive} head come round, very slowly.
{A_nameDef} walked up to {X_indefinite} holding out a turnip, and stood there while {X_pronoun} made up {X_possessive} mind about it.

ColonyCouncil.EncounterDef.label: the beast at the tree line

texts.li: {A_nameDef} saw {X_definite} at the tree line today, in the same spot as on the day of the attack. They looked at each other until {X_pronoun} turned away.
{A_nameDef} dropped a full bucket in the yard and didn't notice. Out past the fence, {X_definite} was pacing slowly back and forth.
Even at that distance, {A_nameDef} knew {X_definite} by the way {X_pronoun} moved, nosing along the tree line as if the land were {X_possessive}.
{A_nameDef} spotted {X_definite} drinking at the far water and came back at a run, leaving the buckets behind.
{A_nameDef} saw {X_definite} in the trees this morning. By noon the news had been round every table, and {A_nameDef} keeps looking over {A_possessive} shoulder.
Since {X_definite} was seen circling the fields again in broad daylight, {A_nameDef} carries a blade even to the latrine.
One moment {A_nameDef}'s hat was on the fence post. The next, {X_indefinite} was carrying it off into the brush.
{A_nameDef} chased {X_indefinite} halfway to the hills for a stolen glove, lost {X_objective} in a thicket, and came back scratched and covered in burrs.
{A_nameDef}'s lunch went missing from the wall where {A_pronoun} had left it, and a trail of crumbs led to {X_indefinite} under a bush.
{A_nameDef} was on {A_possessive} usual midnight walk when {X_indefinite} crossed the path ahead, pale in the starlight, and stopped to look at {A_objective} before going on.
While the others slept, {A_nameDef} sat on the step and watched {X_indefinite} nose around the yard, turning over whatever had been left out.
{A_nameDef} likes the colony best at night. Tonight {X_indefinite} came up close to the doorway where {A_pronoun} sat, and stayed a while.
Heads down, churning the mud to soup, {X_indefinite} and a rival went at each other in the meadow for most of the morning. {A_nameDef} watched until both limped off.
The crack of {X_definite} and a challenger colliding carried all the way from the far fields. {A_nameDef} went out to watch and stayed until it was over.
{A_nameDef} bet a week of washing-up on {X_definite} against the bigger animal, and lost.
